title: House Democrats to Open Majority With Healthcare, Iran War and Tariff Votes
excerpt: When the new Congress convenes on January 3, House Democrats plan first votes to strengthen Medicaid, restore enhanced ACA subsidies, stop the Iran war and reverse some Trump tariffs — with a 60-vote Senate threshold and a presidential veto still in the way.
body:
• House Democrats intend to open their new majority, when Congress convenes January 3, 2027, with votes to strengthen Medicaid and restore the enhanced Affordable Care Act tax subsidies that lower premiums for millions.
  • They also promise swift action on legislation to stop the war with Iran and to reverse some of President Donald Trump's tariffs.
  • Democrats will hold more than 250 of the House's 435 seats; Hakeem Jeffries is expected to seek election as speaker.
  • For ACA enrollees, the reader-relevant fact is timing: the subsidy and Medicaid votes are planned as opening moves, but most legislation still needs 60 Senate votes and could face a Trump veto, so no change takes effect on January 3 itself.

House Democrats will start their majority focused on healthcare. Democratic leaders expect the first votes when the new Congress convenes on January 3 to strengthen Medicaid and restore enhanced tax subsidies that reduce premiums for eligible Affordable Care Act enrollees, the Associated Press reported, in coverage carried by NewsLooks. "We're going to get out of the gate fast," said Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to seek election as speaker.

Healthcare first

Democrats want to reverse Medicaid changes projected to reduce spending by more than $900 billion over a decade. Those changes helped finance Trump's tax and spending legislation enacted last year and imposed additional administrative rules and eligibility conditions, including work requirements. Some of the largest changes have not yet taken effect, but Medicaid enrollment has already fallen by approximately 5 million people, or about 7%, since July 2025, according to KFF. A measure extending enhanced ACA subsidies passed the current House with some Republican support but stalled in the Senate.

Iran and tariffs

Democrats are also promising swift action aimed at stopping the war with Iran and reversing some of Trump's tariffs. Lawmakers have repeatedly considered measures addressing presidential war powers in Iran, with 14 votes in the Senate and six in the House so far. Beyond the opening votes, Jeffries said five working groups are preparing proposals on housing, energy, groceries and caregiving costs, and Democrats intend to scrutinise artificial intelligence and data centre development, as NPR's account of the Democrats' first-100-hours plans also described via WHRO.

"Two things will change next term. We will hold public hearings on AI. We will pass legislation, reasonable guardrails on AI, and specifically data centers."

— Rep. Ted Lieu, Democrat of California

The obstacles

Passage in the House is not in doubt; enactment is harder. Most Senate legislation must clear a 60-vote procedural threshold, requiring Republican cooperation unless Democrats change the rules — progressive groups are pressing leaders to eliminate the filibuster, a step Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer has not committed to. Trump has advertised his willingness to veto legislation, posting an election-night photograph of a red cap bearing the word "VETO." Schumer said his party would pursue its priorities even if Trump opposed them: "If he vetoes it, it will show the divisions." Even unsuccessful votes would define the parties' positions heading into the 2028 presidential election.
